title: The Real Reason Your Food Tastes Bland When You Have a Cold
hook: Your nose is lying to your tongue.

narration.text: When you have a cold, food can taste completely different.
This is because much of what we call taste is actually smell.
Our taste buds only detect five basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami.
But flavour, that rich complex experience, comes from our sense of smell.
When you chew, volatile molecules travel from your mouth to your nasal cavity.
A blocked nose prevents these molecules from reaching your smell receptors.
So, your brain receives less information, making food seem bland.
Next time you are ill, notice how much you rely on smell for flavour.
Have you noticed certain foods tasting different when you have a cold?

description: Ever wondered why your favourite meal loses its magic when you are battling a cold? It is not just your taste buds. Discover the fascinating link between smell and flavour, and why a blocked nose changes your entire eating experience.
topic: Why your perception of taste changes when you have a cold, explaining the role of smell in flavour perception.
